# double-meh-bundler

> Server side of the double-meh bundle protocol: accepts one bundled request (many GETs in one PUT), fans out to backend services, returns all responses in a single compressed envelope. The core is a web-standard fetch handler `(Request) => Promise<Response>`; framework adapters are thin, dependency-free subpaths. Zero runtime dependencies, ESM-only, Node >= 18 / Bun / Deno; the core also runs in service workers and edge runtimes.

## Install

```bash
npm i double-meh-bundler
```

## Core (`double-meh-bundler`)

```js
import {createBundler} from 'double-meh-bundler';

const bundler = createBundler({
  isUrlAcceptable: url => url.startsWith('/api/'), // required — the security boundary
  resolveUrl: url => new URL(url, 'http://api.internal:8080').href
});

Bun.serve({fetch: bundler}); // or Deno.serve(bundler), or any Request → Response host
```

`createBundler(options)` → fetch handler. Options:

- `isUrlAcceptable(url, request)` — required allow-list; unacceptable parts become synthetic 403 parts.
- `resolveUrl(url)` — maps public part URLs to internal ones; default identity.
- `fetch(request)` — injectable upstream fetch; default `globalThis.fetch`.
- `maxRequests` — parts cap per bundle (400 above it); default 20.
- `partTimeout` — per-part upstream timeout in ms; a hung upstream becomes a synthetic 504 part; default 10000.
- `streaming` — answer with `application/vnd.double-meh.bundle+jsonl` when the request's `Accept` names it exactly: a `{"v":1}` header line then one part per line, flushed as upstreams complete. Client-driven, so inert unless asked; disabled whenever `processBundle` is configured. Default true.
- `onBundleStart(context)`, `onItemFinish(part, context)`, `onBundleFinish(bundle, context)` — observers for metrics/logging. Not awaited; a throw or rejection is swallowed — instrumentation never changes behavior. `onBundleFinish` carries the whole-bundle `durationMs` and does not fire when `processBundle` throws.
- `processResult(part, context)`, `processBundle(bundle, context)` — transforms, awaited. A nullish return keeps the original; a throwing `processResult` turns that part into a synthetic 500, a throwing `processBundle` fails the bundle with a 500. `processResult` runs before the base64 sort.

## Node/Express adapter (`double-meh-bundler/node.js`)

```js
import {createServer} from 'node:http';
import {createBundler} from 'double-meh-bundler';
import {toNodeHandler} from 'double-meh-bundler/node.js';

createServer(toNodeHandler(createBundler({isUrlAcceptable}))).listen(3000);
// Express: app.put('/bundle', toNodeHandler(createBundler({isUrlAcceptable})));
```

`toNodeHandler(handler, {compress = true})` → `(req, res, next?)`. Duck-typed: covers bare `node:http` and Express (no framework imports). Gzips the envelope when the client accepts it. Errors go to `next` when present, else 500 problem+json.

## Koa adapter (`double-meh-bundler/koa.js`)

```js
import {toKoaMiddleware} from 'double-meh-bundler/koa.js';

app.use(route.put('/bundle', toKoaMiddleware(createBundler({isUrlAcceptable}))));
```

`toKoaMiddleware(handler)` → `(ctx)`. Terminal middleware (never calls `next`); mount it on the bundle route. Put `koa-compress` in front to compress the envelope.

## Wire format (v1)

- Request: `application/vnd.double-meh.bundle-request+json`, body `{v: 1, parts: [{id, url, method?: 'GET', headers?}]}`; part headers whitelist: `accept`, `accept-language`, `if-none-match`, `if-modified-since`; auth/cookies propagate from the outer request only.
- Response: `application/vnd.double-meh.bundle+json`, body `{v: 1, parts: [{id?, url, status, headers, body?, encoding?, synthetic?}]}`; JSON bodies inline, text as strings, binary as base64 (`encoding: "base64"`) sorted last; 204/304 parts carry no body; per-part failures are `synthetic: true` parts (403 unacceptable, 502 upstream failure, 504 timeout, 405 non-GET); the outer envelope is `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- Streamed response: `application/vnd.double-meh.bundle+jsonl`, JSON Lines — line 1 is `{"v":1}`, every later line is one part in the same v1 shape, in completion order (correlate by `id`). Base64 parts still ship last. `v` stays 1: the framing changed, not the parts.
- Constants exported: `REQUEST_MIME`, `BUNDLE_MIME`, `BUNDLE_JSONL_MIME`. Match content types by essence — `BUNDLE_MIME` is a string prefix of `BUNDLE_JSONL_MIME`, so `startsWith` confuses them.
